title: Flavours of Plenty

hero.alt: Flavours of Plenty festival artwork on a digital screen at the airport baggage claim

intro: Flavours of Plenty is the Coastal Bay of Plenty’s food and drink festival, where the region’s stories come to life over eighteen days of events.
brief: A campaign look for the 2025 festival that could run everywhere at once: digital billboards, the airport, the printed programme, magazines and the festival’s own products.
idea: A cast of characters, each one a flavour of the region: a lemon in sunglasses, a dripping chocolate bar, a kiwifruit couple, an oyster, a bee and its honey. On festival pink they work at any size, from a sticker to an airport screen.

title: Negative Split

hero.alt: Matte black NS disc wheel with oversized gloss lettering

intro: Negative Split Carbon makes carbon wheels for road, tri, gravel and MTB, founded and tested in New Zealand, with a mission to make carbon more accessible.
brief: Wheel graphics for the range: the disc, the tri-spoke and the deep-section rims.
idea: Wheels are seen at speed and from the side of the road, so the NS letters go huge and cropped, wrapping the rim and disc. Gloss on matte black means the graphics catch the light without shouting.

title: Empty Plate Club

hero.alt: Pink Empty Plate Club poster with a walking plate illustration

intro: Empty Plate Club is our own foodie Instagram: home cooking, recipes, snacks and baking, straight from the kitchen.
brief: A name, a character and a look that could hold a feed of very different dishes together, from pasta to pears.
idea: A plate on legs, walking itself home: the whole point of the club in one drawing. Hand-lettered in pink and red, then carried into the profile picture, the pinned post and the highlight covers, so the account feels like a brand rather than a camera roll.

gallery.alt: The Empty Plate Club Instagram grid: a pink pinned logo post above home-cooked dishes

whatWeMade: Highlight covers: Brands, Recipes, Snacks, Baking
result: 90 posts in, one pink system keeps a feed of very different dishes looking like it belongs together.

title: Ride Retreat

hero.alt: A mountain biker lifts his front wheel through tree ferns and redwoods

intro: Ride Retreat is our own premium mountain bike retreat in Rotorua: four days on 200km+ of world-class singletrack, guided by Red Bull pro Brook Macdonald, with a private chef and recovery built into every day.
brief: Build a premium brand from nothing, a website that sells the stay, and a way to look after every guest from the moment they book to the ride home.
idea: Three redwoods and a rider on one wheel sit on top of the wordmark: the whole retreat in one mark, in forest greens and warm yellows. The guest app is a digital concierge for the whole journey, from booking and gear lists to the day-by-day itinerary and the recap afterwards, so the human side of the retreat gets its time back.

result: The guest app has become a case study we present to Rotorua tourism operators: what AI can do for a small operator.

title: Rotorua Walking Tours

hero.alt: Rotorua Walking Tours logo blind-embossed on pink paper

intro: Rotorua Walking Tours shows visitors the city on foot. We gave them a logo and a website to match.
brief: A logo and a website that would make a small, local tour company feel established and easy to book.
idea: A single-line drawing of Rotorua’s landmarks, with a trail of footsteps walking into it. Fine enough to blind-emboss, simple enough to sit at the top of a website.

title: Wings for Life

hero.alt: Yellow street poster of a winged cartoon running on a cloud, headed We’ve got the runs

intro: Creative for a Red Bull athlete’s official Wings for Life World Run campaign, a global run that raises money for spinal cord research.
brief: Get followers to stop scrolling and sign up to run.
idea: A charity run doesn’t have to be earnest. A winged, grinning character and a headline that makes people laugh first, then join.
